import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/test_2.csv"

# Load Source 0
# Schema: ['Rank', 'Code', 'Description', 'x(t)']
# We will keep 'Rank', 'Code', 'Description' from Source0
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
# Confirm columns exist and strip spaces if any
df0.columns = df0.columns.str.strip()
df0 = df0[['Rank', 'Code', 'Description']]

# Load Source 1
# Schema: ['Code', 'Description']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df1.columns = df1.columns.str.strip()
df1 = df1[['Code', 'Description']]

# Load Source 2
# Schema: ['FL_DATE', 'UNIQUE_CARRIER', 'FL_NUM', 'ORIGIN_AIRPORT_ID', 'ORIGIN_CITY_MARKET_ID', 'DEST_AIRPORT_ID', 'DEST_CITY_MARKET_ID']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
df2.columns = df2.columns.str.strip()
# We only need 'DEST_AIRPORT_ID' to join with Code in df0 and df1
df2 = df2[['DEST_AIRPORT_ID']].drop_duplicates()

# --- Transformation Plan ---
# Target schema: ['Code': int, 'Rank': int, 'Description_x': str, 'Description_y': str]
# Target examples show:
# - Code and Rank come from Source0 (df0)
# - Description_x comes from Source0.Description
# - Description_y comes from Source1.Description
# Source2 is used to ensure all Codes in df0 and df1 are valid airport IDs appearing in DEST_AIRPORT_ID.
# We will join df0 and df1 on 'Code' to get Description_y from df1.
# We will filter df0 and df1 Codes to those present in df2.DEST_AIRPORT_ID to ensure consistency with Source2.
# Finally, rename columns to match target schema.

# Filter df0 and df1 to Codes present in df2
valid_codes = set(df2['DEST_AIRPORT_ID'].unique())

df0_filtered = df0[df0['Code'].isin(valid_codes)].copy()
df1_filtered = df1[df1['Code'].isin(valid_codes)].copy()

# Join df0_filtered and df1_filtered on 'Code' to get Description_y from df1
# Left join df0_filtered with df1_filtered to keep all rows from df0_filtered (which has Rank)
df_merged = pd.merge(df0_filtered, df1_filtered, on='Code', how='left', suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Rename columns to target schema
df_merged.rename(columns={
    'Description_x': 'Description_x',
    'Description_y': 'Description_y',
    'Code': 'Code',
    'Rank': 'Rank'
}, inplace=True)

# Select and reorder columns as per target schema
target_df = df_merged[['Code', 'Rank', 'Description_x', 'Description_y']]

# Ensure correct dtypes
target_df['Code'] = target_df['Code'].astype(int)
target_df['Rank'] = target_df['Rank'].astype(int)
target_df['Description_x'] = target_df['Description_x'].astype(str)
target_df['Description_y'] = target_df['Description_y'].astype(str)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
